reviewed_rows.evidence: Direct GetOptionsObject; undefined creates null-prototype object, objects retain identity, other values throw. Captured IsObject/createObject/TypeError contracts remain dependencies.

Shared null-prototype record helper; exact Instant caller shorthand correspondence. Other callers choose unit/smallestUnit and retain their own numbered method steps; no standalone Temporal abstract operation invented.
Rounding-mode table, fallback, ToString and validation kernel. Caller reads roundingMode before entry; source does not itself perform complete GetOption property access.
Normal singular/plural spellings only. Property Get, required/default handling and auto branch belong to callers. Do not map this helper to full §13.17 including auto step8.
Accepts six time units; rejects non-time names. Undefined throws because this fused helper also serves required-unit callers; full §13.18 step1 returns on unset and is explicitly excluded.
Caller owns property Get step1. Kernel defaults undefined then unary-plus Number coercion, truncation, finite/range check and integer return, using trusted captured runtime arithmetic.
Caller owns property Get step1. Kernel maps undefined/auto and numeric finite floor 0..9. Computing floor before finite check adds no visible coercion because numeric branch already primitive.

Exact BigInt quotient/remainder equivalent under positive quantum and validated rounding mode. Correct floor for negative quotient, exact distances/ties/parity. §8.5.7 quantum construction belongs to roundInstantOptions/callers, not this kernel.

Requires already extracted Instant slot. Owns shorthand/options, ordered option reads, time unit validation, inclusive day divisibility, quantum construction and dispatch. Public brand/slot and result construction remain caller responsibilities. Native backend equivalence remains established dependency, not inferred from this mapping.

Signed exact integer rounding implemented via sign reversal and shared positive-mode core; positive quantum and validated mode preconditions. No claim of arbitrary mathematical real input API: private representation is BigInt.
Typed TimeUnit length table; direct table dependency, not full RoundTemporalInstant.
Normal singular/plural six time-unit strings; strip_suffix accepts exact singular/plural only. No auto/default/unset/property Get or ECMAScript coercion ownership.
Exact nine string-to-enum mappings; caller supplies primitive Rust string, ECMAScript coercion/read/fallback remain external.

Positive-sign quotient/remainder arithmetic; i64 fast path uses guarded representable operands and Euclidean division, i128 path otherwise. Quantum1 shortcut exact. Existing caller/domain arithmetic proofs reused; mapping does not promise unrestricted all-i128 values/quanta avoid overflow.

Typed Instant/unit/mode input means public brand, ToNumber, Get and fallback are outside adapter. Enforces nonzero<=1e9 increment, inclusive day bound/divisibility then exact quantum/core and Instant range constructor. Does not claim complete JS Instant.round method.
Signed numerator handling with exact mode reversal. Reuses unsigned core; positive bounded quantum and safely negatable values are caller/domain premises, not unrestricted i128 contract.

Exact floor of BigInt numerator divided by positive divisor; division truncates toward zero, subtract1 exactly iff negative nonmultiple. Dependency of period coordinate and approximation helpers; no standalone Temporal operation or step owner.
Computes greatest base+k*period <= date*day+day-1, positive period; exact BigInt floor dependency. Private chosen-model coordinate; no normative astronomy or independent Temporal operation claimed.

Private consecutive month serial for hostCalendarAddMonths and hostCalendarMonthDifference. Existing finite proof establishes serial adjacency for compact+approximate months and exact Number conversion over supported domain. Links NonISODateAdd implementation-defined provider dependency, not complete date addition.

Safe-integer serial guard, exact BigInt composition, explicit integral epoch guard ±110000400 before exact Number conversion. Supplies Gregorian year estimate to hostCalendarAddMonths; caller corrects to containing calendar year. Not exact inverse to arbitrary epoch or complete NonISODateAdd.

Chosen Chinese/Dangi fallback CalendarYearData partition; hostCalendarYear prefers compact years. Existing finite chronology/precision proof and generated-data joins supply structural contract for NonISOCalendarISOToDate through ISODateToFields step2; does not implement complete date/era field conversion or assert astronomy/ICU parity.
Extracts request.duration JSON field then delegates fixed-field decoding. Private wire property access is not public Temporal field-bag Get; semantics/range checked by Duration::new.

Decodes all ten fixed DURATION_FIELDS using decimal into i128 array, then Duration::new. Decimal-string TS transport preserves exact Number-representable integer value; validation and normalized Number-representable field invariant remain actual Rust owner. No public coercion semantics assigned to serde JSON reads.

Serializes the same ten fixed fields to JSON numbers. Duration::new normalizes stored fields to Number-representable integers, so i128->f64 matches JS field representation. TS createDuration installs brand/result; serializer itself does not implement CreateTemporalDuration or claim public getters/descriptors.

Finite dispatcher owns transport policy: parseDuration bypasses duration input decode; other operations validate duration first; optional relative anchor decodes before operation switch; round decodes largest/smallest/increment/mode; total selects anchored/time/day; subtract boolean chooses checked_subtract. Public callback order belongs TS caller; actual arithmetic/parser owners named separately. No normative algorithm step transplanted onto request dispatch.

Transports already-branded ten-field values plus absolute boolean to typed invoke or FFI; negated/absolute field arithmetic remains Duration::negated/abs. It does not own receiver branding or public construction.

Forwards unchanged prepared primitive string to direct parser or FFI parseDuration; public ToString/ToTemporalDuration dispatch occurs before this adapter. Rust FromStr owns grammar, fraction and sign policy.

Support entrypoint transports a prepared field record through Duration::new and drops successful null result. Current TS Temporal callers validate locally via duration-core.validateDuration; no native validateDuration callsite exists. Interface presence grants no public compliance coverage.

Forwards already-resolved fields/precision/mode; Rust Duration::format owns rounding and FormattedDuration Display owns output. Public options read/validation ordering stays duration.ts; no duplicate ToString algorithm claimed.

Transports one/two validated durations and subtract boolean without inspecting user bags. Rust checked_add/checked_subtract owns arithmetic/range; TS frontend owns ToTemporalDuration order and result creation.

Transports exact fields plus private tagged relative anchor. FFI chooses DurationAnchor::compare or compare_time; zone/calendar/date comparison dependencies remain existing owned algorithms, not generic FFI exemption.

Transports prepared unit and optional relative anchor; no reordering of public option Gets. FFI selects anchored total, exact fixed time total or day total. Result is deliberate mathematical total represented as JS Number, not field integer serialization.

Transports already-resolved largest/smallest/increment/mode and private anchor. FFI selects anchored or no-relative round; owning TS frontend handles user options ordering, Rust rounding engine handles arithmetic/window obligations.
Chosen Chinese/Dangi provider predicate; calendar availability/discovery remains caller policy.
Lazy fallbackLunisolar supplied-data access; pattern performs actual encoding/range decode.
Range-checks integral year index; two captured base64url code units select validated generated dictionary word. Does not validate arbitrary supplied packs or calendar accuracy.
Base29 times12/13 plus popcount of13 length bits; private legal packed-word precondition from shipped generator/validation proof.
Host year data leap ordinal or bundled packed high bits; feeds month-code/month-count callers. No complete Calendar Date Record constructed.
Host/generated first-day data or checkpoint prefix sum; one-past-last year start sentinel supported. Undefined Umm outside chosen starts interval lets caller select civil fallback.
Host prefix differences or29+packed length bit. Caller supplies valid month; undefined Umm outside selected length interval delegates civil fallback.
Host difference from1970/month1 or bundled checkpoint plus year counts/month-1. Exact private coordinate; no whole difference or largestUnit selection.
Host add from1970/month1 or safe nonnegative serial plus greatest checkpoint and bounded year descent; malformed/outside serial fails through existing guards. No day/overflow policy here.

Host conversion or guarded checkpoint/year/month subtraction producing year/month/day. Existing chronology proves forward/inverse for chosen supported data; caller composes era/monthCode and Calendar Date Record.
Selects host coordinate addition or serial-plus-months/inverse; caller owns retained-year monthCode, day constrain/reject and final date conversion.
Difference of consistent month coordinates or host equivalent; caller composes years/weeks/days and largestUnit. No complete NonISODateUntil claim.
Private FIFO insertion cache: captured Map size/keys/iterator-next/delete before set when size>=128. Trusted runtime owns Map/iterator semantics; no calendar calculation or complete Intl audit.

Integral epoch/day range, captured Intl methods and resolved-calendar check, ordered year/day extraction+validation. Supported captured Intl field/data contract supplied; not a complete formatter implementation or arbitrary-provider equivalence proof.

Safe year, captured cache, compact Chinese/Dangi preference then established approximation; Umm reconstructs actual host month starts under supplied Intl field contract. Existing positive partition, continuity, Number bounds and Umm handoff evidence reused.

Finds containing year from exact Gregorian/host estimate then positive start partition month/day. Caller supplies supported integral epoch and composes other Calendar Date Record fields; existing chronology/host contracts reused.

Safe delta plus consecutive month coordinate, bounded inverse estimate and monotone containing-year correction. Existing compact/approximation serial+join proof reused; caller owns date day/overflow policy.
Subtracts exact consecutive coordinates of validated year/month starts. Existing serial adjacency/Number bounds proof reused; duration field decomposition remains caller contract.
Own generated zone names reach fallbackTimeZoneIdentifiers and seed typescriptTimeZone identifier resolution. Caller adds aliases and canonicalizes names.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: decode compact rows for named-zone offset lookup.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.13 step 3.a: keep private offset probes within Instant bounds.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: prepare the host Intl formatter for named offsets.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.9 step 3: decode host ISO clock fields into offset nanoseconds.

reviewed_rows.evidence: Captured native sort orders collected candidate BigInts chronologically. This only maps the comparator, with no completeness claim.
reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.13 step 3.a: sort collected candidates by epoch nanoseconds.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.13 step 3.a: pass the ISO local time as epoch nanoseconds.

reviewed_rows.evidence: Cache predicate requires identical search direction and membership in the cached inclusive query span. Cached result validity remains a caller premise.
reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.3.46 steps 9.a, 10.b: reuse a cached result for this direction and instant.

reviewed_rows.evidence: BigInt quotient with negative nonzero remainder adjustment computes mathematical floor. Used for whole-second probes, including strict previous query after subtracting one nanosecond.
reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.3.46 steps 9.a, 10.b: floor negative and positive probes to whole seconds.

reviewed_rows.evidence: Private predicate checks first ≤ cursor < last for next and first < cursor ≤ last for previous. Span validity and search horizon remain caller premises.
reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §6.3.46 steps 9.a, 10.b: test the directional cached span.
// Proposal comparison §13.35 step 19.b: pad the consumed fraction to nine digits.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The caller reads only the first nine digits. Appending zeros up to width nine yields the same three subfields as appending a full nine zeros. A missing fraction yields zero for all three fields.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.35 step 7: copy bounded field spans from the source string.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Token readers pass bounded spans of the original string. Indexed code-unit copies preserve source text for ASCII numeric fields. This generic helper also serves suffix and annotation callers.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.35 step 4.a.i: split the lexical body from its bracket suffix.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The first left bracket locates where the full suffix starts for the short/date/calendar/time parsing callers. validateAnnotations checks the remaining bracket syntax.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.31 DecimalDigit: recognize one ASCII digit at a bounded index.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Index upper bound and ordered string comparisons delimit exactly ASCII 0 through 9 for token-reader indices.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.31 Date and Time: check fixed-width ASCII digit spans.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Reject overlong reads, then apply DecimalDigit membership to each code unit. Numeric field ranges and end-of-input checks belong to the calling parser.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.31 DateSpec: read year, separators, month and day.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Read four unsigned or six signed year digits and two-digit month/day fields, with consistently present or absent date separators. Negative-zero and Gregorian validity are separate checks.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.31 DateTimeSeparator: accept space, T or t at this index.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Bounded membership test implements the exact lexical separator alternatives. Caller establishes this is the separator position.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.31 DateTime: locate the marker in a parsed zoned body.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The zoned caller uses the lexical separator predicate to distinguish date-only and time-bearing bodies after splitting annotations. Final structural validation stays in parseISODateParts.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.31 UTCDesignator: recognize Z or z.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Strict equality recognizes the two designator alternatives. The calling goal establishes where a designator may occur.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.35 steps 26–26.a: detect a trailing UTC designator in the body.
reviewed_rows.evidence: After splitting annotations, inspect the final code unit as the possible UTCDesignator. The zoned caller checks the time requirement and assembles its result.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.35 step 26: strip a detected designator before field parsing.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Conditional suffix removal is an implementation dependency for reuse of the date-time field scanner in zoned and calendar entrypoints. Callers own grammar acceptance and UTC interpretation.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.31 TimeSpec: capture clock fields, separators and fraction digits.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Read two-digit clock fields with consistent basic/extended separators, accept comma or point for a nonempty seconds fraction, and stop at nine fraction digits. Caller enforces field ranges and rejects excess suffix.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.35 step 27.a: find the end of the numeric offset span.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Locate a signed offset token with two-digit fields and optional fraction, without interpreting it as an offset value. The shared UTCOffsetNanoseconds scanner validates ranges and complete syntax.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.35 step 4.a.i: scan a date-time prefix and keep its suffix.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Collect candidate date/time and offset fields and retain the trailing source for validation. Instant mode requires both clock and offset. This scanner does not decide full parse-goal acceptance.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.31 DateSpecYearMonth: capture the complete short-date body.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Read signed six-digit or unsigned four-digit year and two-digit month, allowing the optional hyphen and requiring end of body. Calendar and month validity are checked by callers.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.31 DateSpecMonthDay: capture the complete month-day body.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Consume optional double-hyphen prefix, two-digit month, optional separator and two-digit day with end-of-body requirement. Caller handles Gregorian validity, calendar restrictions and PlainTime ambiguity.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §3.5.14 steps 8.a, 8.c: represent a plain date at midnight.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The private anchor combines the supplied date and calendar with a zero clock for PlainDate difference. Duration plain-relative preparation reuses this representation.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.13 step 5: preserve the origin date and clock.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Keep the PlainDateTime date with its calendar and exact subday nanoseconds. The origin helper converts this pair to an epoch value.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.12 step 9: supply the anchor calendar to date difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: calendar_difference::date_until obtains the provider through this adapter before calling until_raw. The adapter does not perform CalendarDateUntil.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.13 step 5: compose exact epoch nanoseconds from day and clock.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Exact i128 day-by-day-length multiplication plus stored clock implements the plain-anchor epoch representation for both rounding and total.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.12 steps 5–6: recover the date of each plain endpoint.
reviewed_rows.evidence: calendar_difference::unrounded takes the Euclidean day quotient of both endpoint epochs. The checked narrowing preserves the integer or returns an error. The caller compares dates and chooses the adjustment.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.5.33 steps 8.a–8.c.i, 9–11.a: form plain nudge endpoints.
reviewed_rows.evidence: For date-only nudge fields the helper constrains calendar addition and composes exact day plus the unchanged anchor clock. Shared duration callers also supply a clock span. Duration and date range checks stay explicit, with operation-specific PlainDateTime bounds at the callers.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.15 steps 2, 6: check calendar identity and route the native difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Typed start/end calendar IDs are compared before delegation. The call supplies a PlainDateTime anchor, exact destination, rounding settings and direction. JS option order and result allocation are frontend-owned.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §3.3.25 step 3: route the typed until difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Typed wrapper forwards the two dates and prepared settings with since=false. Receiver slots and public options belong to the frontend.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §3.3.26 step 3: route the typed since difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Typed wrapper forwards the dates and prepared settings with since=true. Shared difference owns directed rounding and negation.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §3.5.14 steps 2, 6–8.e: route the native plain-date difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Check calendar identity and typed date-only unit; shared arithmetic receives midnight origin/destination and requested settings. Settings evaluation and public result creation remain outside this helper.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.21 step 13.h: total a plain-relative span after endpoint checks.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Preserve zero and validate relevant PlainDateTime bounds before exact fixed-unit ratio or shared calendar-relative total. The fixed branch accumulates nanoseconds in i128 before rational_to_f64; no JS coercion or provider-wide claim.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.3.20 step 28.h: round the checked plain-relative endpoints.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Construct the endpoint, enforce lower/upper PlainDateTime bounds on unequal endpoints and delegate exact relative rounding. The helper retains the permitted equal-zero shortcut.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §7.2.3 steps 5.a, 13.b–17: compare exact plain-relative spans.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Equal typed fields return Equal. Only years/months/weeks feed constrained calendar addition; add the integer day delta and compare exact i128 time spans. Frontend conversion and option order remain separate.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §8.5.8 step 4: project the rounded epoch using the supplied offset.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Typed formatter rounds on the requested precision grid, checks the supplied subday offset and projects the integer sum to ISO fields. FFI resolves named offsets from its rounded epoch before invoking this typed formatter. Public options and Instant validity checks remain caller-owned.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §8.5.8 steps 2, 5–6.a: display UTC with automatic precision.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Rust Display defaults to no offset and automatic precision. That path uses an exact unit quantum and delegates to FormattedInstant. This is native rendering correspondence rather than a JS toString entrypoint.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.9 step 7: start an empty buffer for ISO text.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The zero-length byte builder supplies storage for ASCII date-time concatenation. The fixed allocation and initialized tail are private implementation choices.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.9 step 7: append one ASCII byte to the ISO text.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Writes at the initialized prefix boundary and advances its length. Date and clock callers supply literal separators and ASCII digits in their own required order.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.26 steps 2–3, 5: write two decimal digits.
reviewed_rows.evidence: For validated two-digit values, quotient and remainder by ten produce ordered tens and ones digits, including leading zero. Used by date, clock and offset text.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §3.5.10 steps 1, 3: write the year at its selected width.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Repeated decimal remainder fills the selected width from right to left. Callers bound the integer and choose width for year output or the precision-adjusted fractional digits.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.9 steps 1–3: write the year, month and day.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Valid ISO years in 0..9999 use four digits. Other supported years use sign and six-digit absolute magnitude. Hyphens and two-digit month/day form the date prefix. Calendar annotations stay with caller.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.9 steps 5, 7: join the date and clock with T.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Emit ISO date and T, passing existing exact subsecond nanoseconds to the clock writer. This helper produces the ISO portion; calendar annotation remains caller-specific.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §4.5.13 step 2: format a plain clock at the chosen precision.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Allocate the clock output and pass hour, minute, second and the already-combined subsecond integer to append_time. PlainTime rounding occurs before this renderer.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §13.26 steps 2–7: write the clock at the selected precision.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Separated clock form emits HH:MM and optional seconds. Auto removes decimal trailing zeros using exact integer division; fixed precision keeps the requested prefix at exact width. Zero digits omit the dot. Unseparated style is outside this writer.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §5.5.9 step 7: read the completed ISO text prefix.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Read only initialized bytes after ASCII digits and separators have been appended. UTF-8 conversion borrows the completed text and excludes unused storage. This is a representation dependency.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §8.5.8 steps 5–8: append Z or the rounded offset to the ISO text.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Serialize supplied fields with no calendar suffix, then append Z for absent offset or sign plus hour/minute from rounded offset minutes. Named offset lookup occurs before this writer.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.7 steps 1–2: round a signed offset to whole minutes.
reviewed_rows.evidence: For bounded offsets, add half a minute to absolute nanoseconds, divide by one minute and restore sign. Exact integer arithmetic implements half-expand including ties and normalized zero.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §11.1.7 step 3: write the rounded offset as signed hours and minutes.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Zoned renderer passes the actual offset when showOffset applies. Sign and two-digit hour/minute fields follow quotient and remainder of absolute rounded minutes. Zero emits plus.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §3.3.3 step 3: read the selected provider's calendar ID.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Matches on the already-selected enum variant and returns its provider ID. Calendar selection, canonicalization and string conversion are outside the trait method.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.26 steps 1.b, 2: project a short-date reference day.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Dispatches an epoch day through the extended provider projection. Short-date reference days and merge-field preparation can use the wider conversion window. Short-date callers own object limits.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.13 step 3: convert fields to a year-month reference day.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Dispatches selected year, ordinal month, day and overflow to the extended provider inverse. YearMonth/MonthDay reference-day generation and final bounds remain caller policies.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §9.5.8 step 12: dispatch year-month addition to the provider.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The typed short-date caller selects a first day and range policy before invoking this arithmetic delegate. The wrapper forwards epoch, duration and overflow unchanged.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §9.3.4 and §9.3.5 step 3: project era fields at the reference day.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Returns provider era data for extended YearMonth reference days. Underlying arithmetic/table provider decides era identity or absence.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.26 steps 1.b, 2: convert an epoch day through its calendar.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Dispatches the normal-range epoch day to the selected provider. The provider computes date fields, while callers assemble any additional Calendar Date Record fields.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.22 steps 1.b, 2: convert resolved fields to an epoch day.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Dispatches resolved year, ordinal month and day with overflow to the selected provider. The provider implements regulation/inverse conversion; the adapter applies no second policy.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.31 steps 1.h, 2.a: resolve a month code through its calendar.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Forwards an already parsed month code, year and overflow to the provider. Ordinal consistency with an explicit month belongs to resolve_year_month.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §3.3.17 step 3: read the provider's month count for this year.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Dispatch returns the selected provider’s month count for the projected year. Public getter numeric representation and receiver validation remain separate.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §3.3.15 step 3: read the provider's day count for this month.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Dispatch returns the selected provider’s month length after the caller extracts its year and month. The public ISO/calendar field getter owns projection and output.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §3.3.11 step 3: supply the year start for the day-of-year count.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Supplies start_of_year through the actual provider. PlainDate subtracts this boundary for dayOfYear; PlainYearMonth subtracts consecutive boundaries for daysInYear.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §3.3.4 and §3.3.5 step 3: read provider era fields.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Dispatches normal-range era lookup, returning optional era name/year from the selected provider. Absence and conversion to public fields remain caller-owned.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.31 step 2.a: resolve a non-ISO era and era year.
reviewed_rows.evidence: The typed year-resolution path passes an existing era/year pair to the selected provider. Conversion rejects provider-invalid era input and the caller separately checks explicit year agreement.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.7 steps 1, 2.a: dispatch checked calendar date addition.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Dispatches the normal-range day, date duration and overflow. Arithmetic and table variants own their add algorithms; caller/owner handles final range checks.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.9 steps 3, 4: dispatch calendar date difference.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Forwards the two epoch-day endpoints and largest date unit to the chosen provider. The adapter establishes neither ISO maximal-prefix equivalence nor any provider-wide difference claim.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.5 step 1: check whether typed date updates contain fields.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Only measures presence of supported typed date fields. Era fields do not count in the ISO, Chinese or Dangi paths. It does not collect a spec List or read JS object properties.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.5 steps 1–6: merge typed overrides with the projected date.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Apply field shape, skip unsupported era updates and reject empty updates. Preserve non-overridden date fields, clearing the old month code for an explicit month and the base year for supported year/era updates. The typed helper supplies existing with-method callers; frontend owns public data reads.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.22 steps 1.b, 2: carry date conversion errors to callers.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Used by resolve_fields after provider date-to-epoch conversion. Retains out-of-range and invalid-duration categories and maps other calendar errors to the typed invalid-date variant. JS exception construction lies across the frontend boundary.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.12 step 2: pass the prepared overflow mode to date conversion.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Preserves an already-selected overflow enum through a two-variant conversion. No options read, parsing or constraint arithmetic happens in this helper.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.12 steps 1–2: resolve typed fields and convert the date.
reviewed_rows.evidence: First resolves the typed calendar year/month, requires a day, then calls provider date conversion with the chosen overflow. Object construction and frontend error precedence remain separate.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.31 step 2.a: reconcile typed year and era fields.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Ignores era fields for ISO, Chinese and Dangi. Otherwise requires an era/eraYear pair if either is present, converts the pair through the provider, and checks matching explicit year. Calendar policy and initial property reads remain separate.

reviewed_rows.annotation: // Proposal comparison §12.3.31 steps 1.e, 1.g–h, 2.a: resolve typed year and month.
reviewed_rows.evidence: Requires resolved year and month or monthCode for the typed callers, rejects nonpositive explicit month/day and checks numeric month agreement with the provider’s selected code. Provider owns the lookup and public frontend owns field coercions.
